data.translation: mit den Worten: »Knüpfe es, was es auch sei, an das Ende dieses Gürtels«. Der Kaufmann band es fest, und Sîne zog den Gürtel hinauf, dann löste sie das Ding vom Gürtel ab,

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Lo yaho! Atənone ʕamuqe bi arʕo, kqəṭrənne hawxa, kməqḏənne, kətte nuqro ste laǧan u hno, laǧan u qaṭmo d nofəq biya. Eee... hul d mafšəriwo ak kefe.
data.translation: Father Brahim: No, my boy! Small kilns deep in the earth; they build them like that, they burn them; it also has a hole for the thing, for the ash which comes out through it. Yes... until they made the stones disintegrate.

rationale: Thin architectural sense cell after round 1; kiln construction supplies a distinct contextual contrast with digging/building or burning. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

data.turoyo: ŭ maʕlə́nwayle lálʕalste, qŭṭríwayle ṭowo, ṭoranwayle šəbbak̇e, dgoraš hăwa, ŭ ǧŭġríwayle, lăǧan dmaḥti nuro bgawe.
data.translation: and they would also raise it upwards, they roofed it well, they would leave it some windows, so that it draws air, and they would ignite it, in order to make fire inside it.

rationale: Thin I.2 Infectum-wa cell; roof construction in kiln-making.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/111)

data.turoyo: Masríwanne ʕam ḥḏoḏe, saymíwanne tăqəm bu+ḥawlo, ḥa ḥawlo ʕal qarʕe d̥kulle, kul+ḥa quṭríwayle bu+ḥawlawo, kul+ḥa quṭriwa u+qamoyo, hul d̥saymiwa qaṭro+ḥreno dmabərmile bəqḏole d̥awo.
data.translation: They would tie them together, they would make them into a squad with rope, one rope on everyone’s heads, each one they would bind with that rope, each one, they would tie the first one, until they made another knot which they twist around the neck of that one.

rationale: Empty I.1 Infectum-wa cell; explicit animal-binding procedure, both target tokens in one context.

data.translation: they would twist three whatsits around our heads, and tie them here, and our head would became like so

data.translation: Es gab etwas, das man markno nannte, es war aus Dingsda, aus Ton, sehr groß. Darin machten sie Joghurt aus der Milch. Er war sehr groß

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum-wa cell; overt milk object and earthenware location.

data.turoyo: Kətle ḥdudat, məqqayṣ kətle ḥdud. Qəṭʕiwo aṭ ṭarošaṯṯe, rayziwonne ʕal ḥḏoḏe. Hul d nəšfiwo. Annaqqa maltəmiwo kefe w ḥəfriwo u atuno, manḏ̣əfiwole w maʕməriwole w qəṭriwole w nəšfiwo aṭ ṭarfe. Annaqqa ḥa lalyo saymiwo, lalyo w imomo, ǧəġriwole ann arbaʕ w ʕəsri saʕat.
data.translation: It has boundaries, each one has a boundary. They cut its scrubwood, piled it up, until it dried. Then they gathered stones and dug out the kiln, cleaned it and built it up and constructed it, and the leaves dried. Then they did it for a night, night and day, they fired it for those twenty-four hours.

rationale: Thin architectural sense cell after round 1; kiln construction supplies a distinct contextual contrast with digging/building or burning. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.31/5014)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Aḥna meqəm, əzzənwo ḥor! Məbliwo karəwono, ya ḥatro, xurziwola bi arʕo bayn daz zadone, quṭriwo aʕla čike d Ṣiboro, əmmiwo: "Dəm barxo, d Aloho d amṭe aʕla, maḥfaḏla man afat di šato"... hayo yo, haṯe yo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: We formerly, they used to go, look! They would take a plough beam or a stick, thrust it into the ground among the crops, tie a little Annunciation thread to it, and say, “That it may be blessed, that God may bring upon it, preserve it from the year’s calamities”... That is it, this is it.

rationale: Infectum-wa tying has two round-1 examples; adds a ritual thread and explicit aʕla attachment target without a new sense. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: The dairy alternation is lexical I curdling versus causative III making milk set. JTM 2.5/2 remains active III although the edition renders one repeated clause as a passive. No new dairy sense is required.

Architectural descriptions consistently distinguish active masons from roof/frame patients in Detransitive forms. b- marks materials and ʕal the formwork/support; source and goal footings occur in arch construction. The foundation arch specialisation remains under I.2.
Assimilated qṭəlle/qṭəlla in tying contexts belongs to qṭr, not qṭl. Preterit qṭirile with L-agent and objects must not be conflated with unsuffixed Detransitive qṭīr.
Rope-tying of animals and scarves fills I.1 Infectum-wa, while masonry fills I.2 and 2b. The root already has that box under curdling; these are missing sense cells, not a newly discovered box.
I.4 Triebe ansetzen is preserved; no supplied occurrence bears on it. No idiom or contact claim is inferred.

Jan’s kiln uses reinforce inherited I.2 and round-1 roofing/arching evidence. The 2b foundation-arch proposal is retained, but no explicit qəšto or joined footings in these Jan clauses warrants that narrower label.
Annunciation-thread tying retains literal I.1; its ritual purpose does not create an idiom or a crop-protection sense of the verb.

mqaṭre occurs as a gloss of Distrek with water vapour, dripping and arak. Distillation as a topic is secure; a productive native II verbal series is not. No finite II form or reconstructed base is published.
Confirm qṭīr as Detransitive Preterit versus a state expression, while plural qṭire is filed as Part. Pass.; recordings would settle vowel length/stress.
Check maqəḏ̣alle in PrS 78/22 against the edition before assigning qṭr III, another root, person or box. No supplied spelling is corrected.
Confirm feminine qəṭrowa after masculine howewa in JL 12.14/3, and final -e in Qṭare as object morphology.
Check instrumental dad+dafe dəqṭərre at Material culture/76 and the explicitly repaired temporal clause in /68; neither justifies normalizing the transcript.
Verify inherited PrS page/line aliases for the already quoted bear-tying sequence at PrS 32/9; no citation replacement is inferred from the numbering difference.
Jan 2.12/3216: is mqaṭre a code-switched Arabic/learned adjective or an integrated Turoyo II Part. Pass.? Supply finite native forms before establishing that stem.
Jan 2.12/3263,3275: confirm what part of the kiln qəṭriwole/kqəṭrənne constructs, specifically whether roofing or vaulting; the provisional I.2 filing follows the architectural baseline.
All English beside Jan examples is supplied project machine translation, including its generic “constructed/build” wording; it does not establish a general building sense.
Remove the duplicated pronoun
rationale: The clause already has the subject er and object sie. The first sie is accidentally duplicated.

summary: Jan’s kiln clauses support the established roofing construction. The operation follows digging, cleaning and building, so do not broaden qṭr into a general “bauen” verb; exact superstructure remains to be checked.
